auditMethod: candidate JSON versus fixed Gold JSON/spec; semantic equivalence reviewed by Codex; source PDFs reread only to resolve disputed Gold/candidate interpretations

reasons: The candidate materially contains the Gold triple module, associated algebra, evaluation/Khovanov comparison, Theorem 4.1 gluing isomorphism, and all three handle formulas with their hypotheses.
paper:theorem:4.1 is semantically equivalent to the Gold main target despite identifier and title differences.
The glue/cut construction, isotopy well-definedness, bimodule balancing, and handle specializations preserve a more detailed version of the Gold proof spine.
The B0 boundary includes evaluation and Khovanov inputs but omits the Gold MWW foundation and Ren-Willis gluing-surjection boundary as distinct entries, while adding prior handle-formula results.
Duplicate summary/proof nodes and one malformed formula lower object/source credit but do not erase the represented mathematics.
The cornered category/bimodule, tensor product, HH0 self-gluing, trisection presentation, surface bicategory, and three-manifold gluing families are materially present.
paper:theorem:gluing is the theorem numbered 3.8 and is semantically equivalent to the Gold main target.
The candidate preserves the two-piece gluing to self-gluing to trisection chain and the independent two-dimensional gluing chain, though some intermediate dependencies are compressed.
Ren-Willis and fragmentation are represented in B0; MWW and Gay-Kirby are not represented as the distinct Gold boundary inputs, and MN22 is added.
Number-based identifiers and a malformed Hochschild identifier reduce presentation quality but not semantic coverage.

The candidate has broad coverage of Heegaard/trisection definitions, Morse 2-functions, relative and group trisections, bridge position, Lefschetz fibrations, triangulation algorithms, and generalized trisections.
It selects bridge position rather than the fixed Gold Gay-Kirby existence/stable-uniqueness target, so main-target credit is zero under the current benchmark.
Gay-Kirby and several surveyed results are placed in B0, but Freedman, Donaldson, and CGP are missing as distinct Gold boundary entries and the B0 set is over-expanded.
Most emitted relations are organizational/definitional rather than invented theorem proofs, but a few survey associations remain noisier than the Gold graph with no inferences.
The current Gold imposes a single target on a multi-topic survey; this is a benchmark-design caveat, not a reason to silently change this run's score.
The candidate represents the 2-handle-neighborhood definition, Lemma 2.6, Bauer and Froyshov inputs, Theorems 2.8, 2.3 and 2.4, Lemma 3.1, and the two introductory consequences.
paper:theorem:1.4 is exactly the fixed Gold main target.
The sphere construction, nonvanishing/vanishing contradiction, positive-definite conclusion, and symplectic-orientation obstruction are connected in the correct direction.
All four Gold B0 families are materially represented, but the boundary is over-expanded with duplicate Taubes, Bauer, and Froyshov nodes.
Duplicate theorem nodes and PDF text corruption in a few formulas prevent full object, dependency, state, and source credit.

summary.decision: V3 is runnable and semantically stronger than its automatic matcher scores indicate; next optimization should target aggregation, deduplication, B0 normalization, and survey target selection.
